title: Q-RULEREFS-deploy-revert: a push to main deploys with no probe-driven rollback; site/probes.json (mode revert) has no reader
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** rulerefs audit 2026-11-25 (RULE-REFS-1): the public revert claim was bound to a config file no pipeline reads
**Done check:** cmd:git grep -qF probes.json -- .github/workflows/deploy-ultrastable.yml
**Status:** open

code-task: repo=ultrastable/ultrastable path=.github/workflows/deploy-ultrastable.yml
Rollback on a failed live check exists on one path only: a pull request with the `handoff` label and a verify line (seed/worker/src/handoff.js, site/deployer.js /__internal/rollback, test 'a red probe rolls the deploy back and puts the item back to ready'). The push-to-main path (deploy-ultrastable.yml, deploy/deploy-oidc.mjs, deploy/deploy-workers.mjs) deploys and probes and does not roll back. site/probes.json declares `mode: revert` and the probes that must keep passing, and nothing in .github/workflows or deploy/ reads it; only the adapter template workers/adapters/github/workflows/canonical-deploy.yml and the reference scripts do. The site copy was changed on 2026-11-25 to say what the code does (handed-off changes). Make the stronger sentence true: after deploy-oidc.mjs, run the probes in site/probes.json against the live site and, when one fails twice, call the site worker's rollback route for the workers just deployed and reopen the item; add the test; then the site may say every deploy again, bound to that test.

size: M

**Closing probe:** cmd:git grep -qF probes.json -- .github/workflows/deploy-ultrastable.yml ; the deploy workflow reads site/probes.json and a test proves a failing probe rolls the deploy back.


**Prediction:** spec_quality >= 0.7 within 336 h (read by `python3 -m foundation specgate --report`; this item closing by its done check keeps the share of well-specified open items at or above today's reading)

**Out of scope:** deleting the rule that names the reference, or adding the reference to the excuse list in doctrine/rule-refs.json.
